findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a CI repo uses `runner = "windows-latest"`, a separate Linux `test_runner`, and one group.
This branch selects the grouped workflow for that configuration. Its result job runs on `runner`, but the command at `src/forge/prcheck.py:127` is Bash syntax and does not specify a shell. [GitHub Actions defaults to PowerShell on Windows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax), so the required `tests` check fails even for a docs-only PR or a passing test group. The previous one-group result ran on the Linux test runner.
findings.title: Keep the required result job executable on Windows

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - Forge runs its nightly or release full test suite.
`tests/test_pull_request_test_machines.py:17-18` already tests one group with distinct runner labels, but lines 55-58 expect no `docs-check` or `tests-passed` jobs unless there are multiple groups. This change generates both jobs for that case, so that existing test will fail and keep the full suite red.
findings.title: Update the existing one-group runner test

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a repo with a `.forge/always-tests.txt` list opens a documentation-only PR.
The shipped classifier at `src/forge/templates/review-tests.py:173-177` clears `docs_only` when that list is populated. The grouped workflow then starts its `tests` job on `test_runner` at `src/forge/prcheck.py:83-90`, so the fast runner is still occupied. Forge itself has this list, and `src/forge/templates/brief.md:408-411` says its required tests run on documentation-only changes; those tests still need to run while honoring the requested runner allocation.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a docs-only PR is scheduled or an existing repo runs sync after upgrading.
The scheduling assertion only looks for the docs-only comparison in the job text. Changing the condition's `&&` to `||` would schedule the fast job for every PR while this test still passes. The sync loop at lines 35-39 also starts with the already-correct workflow written by init, so it would pass if sync stopped replacing existing workflows. The named proof therefore does not establish either scheduling or the existing-repo sync behavior.

why: With one test group, a docs-only pull request still runs its tests result job on the fast test runner, so it takes a fast slot from real test work
